what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/write-from-a-recipe: the instruction a person's AI writes from, built from a writing recipe, the check of what it wrote against that recipe, and the list of kept recipes and instruction blocks.

payload.label: Check writing from a file
payload.job: Check a source backed writing request from a file the person granted to be read, without sending the source bytes in the tool call
payload.description: Give file (a relative path in the folder you granted the tool to read), and optionally recipe_id or recipe to override the request's recipe. The file is bounded to 8 MiB and must be a regular JSON file inside the granted folder. It uses the same writing gate as tool:check-writing-against-its-recipe and returns only that gate result; the file contents are not returned.

file.description: A relative path to the request JSON inside the granted folder

recipe_id.description: Optional recipe id; overrides recipe_id in the file

recipe.description: Optional recipe; overrides recipe in the file

provenance.source: The existing check-writing-against-its-recipe gate, with file access constrained to the person's explicit folder grant.

payload.label: Build the instruction to write from
payload.job: Build the exact instruction to write something from a writing recipe and the person's material, before writing it
payload.description: Give recipe_id (from tool:list-writing-recipes) or your own recipe (instruction_plan.prompt_template: literal text, { block_ref }, { slot: work_item, path }, { slot: schema }, { slot: grounding, label } and conditional segments; optional output_contract, gate_policy, delivery_target, context_retrieval, work_item fields), work_item (the person's text and the answers the recipe asks for; missing answers take the recipe's defaults), grounding (source excerpts, each with its id) and blocks (your own instruction blocks, replacing kept ones of the same id). Returns instruction_text to write from, input_refs, output_kind, output_schema, and the recipe's gate_policy and delivery_target. Write from instruction_text yourself, then hand what you wrote to tool:check-writing-against-its-recipe. Nothing here writes or sends anything.

recipe_id.description: A kept recipe's id, like writing-recipe:summarize

recipe.description: Your own writing recipe instead of a kept one

work_item.description: The text to work on (text) and the answers the recipe asks for

grounding.description: Source excerpts the writing may cite, each with its id

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/content-generation compose-run-request-lib.mjs (unchanged), with the recipes of packages/content-actions and the instruction blocks of packages/ai-instruction-blocks; the dispatch to an AI producer was not carried: the person's own AI writes

work_item.text: Book the hall. Maybe think about snacks someday. Send the invites by Friday.

payload.label: Check writing against its recipe
payload.job: Check something written from a recipe before it goes anywhere: it cites only the sources given, it keeps the recipe's rules and reviews, and it is shaped for the next tool
payload.description: Give recipe_id or recipe (as tool:compose-a-writing-instruction took), writing (the JSON object you wrote in the recipe output shape), grounding, work_item, context and review. For ordinary recipes, review is { accepted, verdicts: [{ id, accepted }] }. For an opt-in gate_policy.evidence_contract of source-backed-claims/v1, also give evidence_packet with exact source editions, claims, scopes and UTF-8 quote spans; writing must include exact draft_text and matching claim refs/version/text/scope/source_refs. Semantic review then binds each required verdict to the exact draft, claim version and scope, and source edition set. Reviewer attribution is caller-supplied and is reported unverified; it is not authenticated. Rights metadata is preserved but does not authorize publication. Checks stop at first refusal, then build one delivery request for the named owner tool. A refusal has no delivery.

writing.description: What the AI wrote, as a JSON object

evidence_packet.description: For source-backed-claims/v1 recipes: schema, sources [{ref, edition_id, origin_ref, source_text, content_identity, rights}], and claims [{ref, version_id, text, scope, evidence_refs [{source_ref, edition_id, content_identity, relation, quote}]]}. Source rights are metadata only.

context.description: Values the delivery input may take from context

review.description: Ordinary: {accepted, verdicts}. Strict evidence review: {accepted, attribution:{reviewer_ref, method}, binding:{draft_identity,claim_set_identity,source_set_identity,claims:[{claim_ref,claim_version_id,claim_identity,scope_identity}]}, verdicts:[{id,accepted,claim_ref,claim_version_id,claim_identity,scope_identity,draft_identity,claim_set_identity,source_set_identity,rationale}]}. Attribution remains caller-provided and unauthenticated.

review_binding.description: When a strict semantic review is missing or stale, the exact draft, claim set and source edition identities to review.

evidence_review.description: Successful strict checks mark reviewer attribution caller_attributed_unverified and rights metadata_preserved_not_authorized.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/content-generation gate-and-build-owner-delivery-lib.mjs and its command (the source checks, the required verdicts and the handoff builder); its word checks are tools/judge-words rows

payload.label: Writing recipes and instruction blocks
payload.job: List the ready writing recipes (summarize, translate, rewrite, critique and more) and the instruction blocks a recipe can use
payload.description: Give words (every word must be in a recipe's or block's id or label) and section to narrow the list, or nothing for all. Returns recipes, each with id, label, section, needs (the work item fields it must have) and fields (the answers it asks for, with choices and defaults), blocks (id, label, body) and sections. Use a recipe's id as recipe_id in tool:compose-a-writing-instruction.

provenance.source: the action rows of bitfield-packages packages/content-actions and the blocks of packages/ai-instruction-blocks, kept as DATA here
